explore_lenses.label: What do the released records say about changed votes?
explore_lenses.title: Capability and access are not proof of altered results
explore_lenses.summary: The administration says the declassified material shows foreign adversaries, including China, could compromise election-related systems and that China acquired voter data. claims.text: The White House says the released intelligence assesses that Russia, China, Iran, North Korea and some nonstate groups have the capability to compromise election infrastructure, with voter-registration databases, pollbooks and official election websites identified as particularly vulnerable to disruption.

The National Intelligence Council reports described by ABC say manipulation of vote-tabulation systems at a scale sufficient to change an outcome would be difficult to coordinate and that post-election audits and paper trails would very likely expose it.

Trump argues that China acquired 220 million voter files and that intelligence officials suppressed the scope of Chinese interference; China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian called the allegations fabricated and denied interference in U.S. elections.
Neither the speech nor the reporting on the released materials supplied specific evidence that foreign actors changed votes or the 2020 election result.

explore_lenses.label: Who faces the greatest smoke-health risk?
explore_lenses.title: Risk is uneven, but exposure can affect anyone
explore_lenses.summary: Wildfire smoke can travel far from the fires and contains fine particle pollution that can worsen health quickly. People with existing heart or lung disease and those with greater exposure need particular caution.

claims.text: CDC identifies people with asthma, COPD, heart disease, diabetes or kidney disease; children; pregnant people; and responders as groups at increased risk from wildfire smoke.

EPA says smoke can travel hundreds to thousands of miles, and short-term exposure is associated with effects ranging from eye and respiratory irritation to exacerbation of respiratory and cardiovascular disease.
For exposure reduction, CDC advises limiting time outdoors, using a cleaner indoor room or air filtration, and using a properly fitted NIOSH-approved N95 outdoors when exposure cannot be avoided.
Local conditions can change quickly; EPA directs residents to use AirNow’s current and forecast AQI and Fire and Smoke Map rather than assuming conditions are uniform across a city or region.

explore_lenses.label: How was the 278,000 estimate produced?
explore_lenses.title: The two figures combine different data reviews
explore_lenses.summary: The administration’s 278,000 figure appears to combine its claim of more than 250,000 potential noncitizens in four states with 28,000 more in 23 cooperating states. The central dispute is not whether noncitizens may ever appear on rolls, but whether the matching process reliably establishes citizenship and registration status.

claims.text: DHS’s July 17 letters described the four-state counts as preliminary and listed up to 190,832 potential noncitizens in California, 35,152 in New Jersey, 15,903 in Nevada, and 14,576 in Pennsylvania.

Mullin said DHS had identified an additional 28,000 noncitizens among 23 states using the federal SAVE system; added to the four-state claim, that accounts for the approximately 278,000 total cited by Trump.

A White House official said the four-state estimate relied on commercial-database analysis. David Becker of the Center for Election Innovation and Research said this kind of matching is likely to create false positives, including eligible voters.

stories.summary: Italian officials have received prison sentences related to the 2018 collapse of the Morandi Bridge in Genoa, which resulted in 43 fatalities. Giovanni Castellucci, the former head of Italy's motorway operator, was sentenced to 12 years in prison for his role in the disaster.
